keys.intro: The secret GPG keys of your keyring (~/.gnupg). The repositories are signed with them, and whoever uses a repository installs its public key.
keys.working: Working with gpg. Making a key can take a minute.
keys.empty: There is no secret GPG key in your keyring. Make a new one, or import one from a file.
keys.noPassphraseHint: Anyone who gets a copy of your keyring can sign with this key.
keys.inUse: It signs {repos}: it cannot be deleted.
keys.name: Name
keys.typeNote: The key is RSA 4096, which every version of apt can check.
keys.withoutPassphraseWarning: Without a passphrase, the key can sign with nobody typing anything, which helps to automate. But anyone who gets a copy of your keyring can sign packages as your repository.
keys.passphraseMismatch: The two passphrases are not the same.
keys.exportText: The public key is the one that whoever uses the repository installs. It holds nothing secret.
keys.exportAscHint: To publish it on a web page or send it.
keys.backupText: The file holds the secret key: whoever has it can sign as your repository. Keep it where only you can reach it. If the key has a passphrase, gpg asks for it.
keys.deleteText: The secret and the public key are deleted from your keyring. Without a backup, it cannot be undone.
keys.alreadyThere: The key was already in your keyring.
keys.noSecret: The file had no secret key. A public key alone cannot sign.
keys.backedUp: The backup is saved. Only your user can read it.

repos.intro: The APT repositories that the program keeps. The one in use is where packages are added and what is published.
repos.working: Working on the repository. Signing it can ask for the passphrase of the key.
repos.empty: There is no repository yet. Make a new one in an empty folder.
repos.keyMissing: Its key is not in your keyring
repos.keyMismatchHint: The settings of reprepro sign with {key}, which is not the key of this repository.
repos.name: Name
repos.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It cannot be changed later.
repos.title: Title
repos.titleHint: It goes in the Origin and Label of the repository, which apt shows.
repos.folderHint: A new or empty folder: the repository is made inside it.
repos.noKeys: There is no key to sign with.
repos.keyChangeHint: The repository is signed again with the new key, and its public.key changes: whoever uses it will have to install the new public key.
repos.removeText: The repository leaves the list. Its folder and its packages stay on the disk, and it can be added again.
repos.bashScriptHint: Run this script with bash on any Debian/Ubuntu system to install the GPG key and enable the repository.

packages.noRepo: There is no repository in use. Choose one in the sidebar, or make one in Repositories.
packages.empty: The repository has no packages. Drop .deb files or whole folders on the window to add them.
packages.dropHint: You can also drop .deb files or whole folders on the window: every package inside them is found, in every subfolder.
packages.dropHere: Drop to check the packages for {repo}
packages.republishHint: Prepares the data for the software centers, signs and publishes the repository, without adding anything
packages.otherRepos: The states above are the ones of {repo}. Every other repository only gets the packages it does not have at the same or a newer version.
packages.noGit: {repos}: no Git address, so it is updated on this computer and not published. Set it in Repositories.
packages.historyWarning: {repos}: this first time, its Git history is replaced by the files of now, in one commit. apt does not notice; whoever cloned it has to clone it again.

stage.store: {repo}: preparing the data for the software centers
stage.signing: {repo}: signing. It can ask for the passphrase of the key.

packages.resultLine: Added: {added}. Already there, same or newer: {skipped}.
packages.notPublishedNoGit: Not published: it has no Git address.
packages.removeText: The package leaves {repo}, and its file is deleted from the pool. The repository is signed and published again.

status.noSection: No Section or Priority: reprepro would skip it

packages.republishConfirmText: Do you want to regenerate metadata, sign with GPG, and publish repository {repo} to Git?

build.intro: Make a Debian package from a program. With the desktop integration it gets its menu entry, its icon and the metainfo the software centers read, all named by the same id, and it is checked when it is built.

kinds.fileHint: A binary or a script, installed as /usr/bin/<name>.
kinds.folderHint: A program with its own files, installed in /opt/<name> with a launcher in /usr/bin.
kinds.treeHint: A folder laid out as the system (usr/, etc/…), copied as it is.

build.entryHint: Relative to the folder. The launcher /usr/bin/{name} runs it.
build.name: Package name
build.descriptionPlaceholder: What the program does. An empty line starts a new paragraph.
build.maintainerHint: It is remembered for the next package.
build.desktopHint: Menu entry, icon in every size of the theme and AppStream metainfo, so the program shows in the menu and in software centers.
build.missing: Fill in the program, name, version, summary, maintainer and folder (and the id and name of the menu entry).
build.existsText: {folder} already has a package with this name, version and architecture.

cleanup.intro: Repository maintenance and cleanup. Allows emptying existing packages to start fresh or resetting Git history.
cleanup.normalCleanDesc: Removes all packages and metadata (pool, dists, media, appstream) while keeping configuration (conf/distributions, GPG keys) intact and publishes the change preserving commit history.
cleanup.confirmNormalText: This action will remove all .deb packages from the repository while keeping keys and configuration. It will be published as a commit in the current history.
cleanup.deepCleanDesc: Removes all packages from the repository and squashes Git history into a single clean initial commit. Reduces local and remote repository size to the absolute minimum.
cleanup.confirmText: This action will remove all packages and reset Git history to a single empty commit. The repository will be reset to zero, ready for new packages.

check.intro: Look at .deb packages before publishing them: what reprepro and GitHub would refuse, and what software centers need to show the program. Nothing is changed.
check.emptyDesc: Or add them with the buttons above. Folders are gone through with every folder inside them.
check.sendToRepo: Add {count, plural, one {# package} other {# packages}} to {repo}
check.noRepo: Choose a repository in the sidebar first
check.withLintian: Also run lintian (slow with large packages)

items.notADeb: It is not a Debian package that dpkg can read.
items.missingField: The control file has no {field} field.
items.missingRepreproField: No {field} field: reprepro would skip the package with only a line in its output.
items.maintainer: The Maintainer field is missing or has no e-mail address.
items.badVersion: {version} is not a valid Debian version.
items.archNotInRepo: The architecture {arch} is not in the repository in use ({list}).
items.tooBig: {size} MiB: GitHub refuses files over 100 MiB.
items.notExtracted: The package could not be unpacked to look at its desktop files.
items.noDesktopApp: No menu entry or metainfo: it is not a desktop program (a library, a kernel, a theme…).
items.execOutside: {desktop} starts {program}, which this package does not install.
items.iconFound: The icon {icon} is in the package.
items.iconMissing: The icon {icon} of {desktop} is not in the package.
items.noMetainfo: No AppStream metainfo: software centers will not show it.
items.noDesktop: It has metainfo but no menu entry.
items.noLaunchable: {file} has no launchable: software centers cannot open the program.
items.launchableOk: The metainfo points to {desktop}, which is in the package.
items.launchableMissing: The metainfo points to {desktop}, which is not in the package: software centers cannot link it to the menu entry.
items.screenshots: The metainfo has {count, plural, one {# screenshot} other {# screenshots}}.
items.releaseMismatch: The latest release of the metainfo is {release}, but the package is {version}.
items.releaseOk: The latest release of the metainfo matches the version.
items.appstreamErrors: appstreamcli finds {count, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}} in {file}.
items.lintianWarnings: lintian: {count, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}.
items.lintianErrors: lintian: {errors, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}} and {warnings, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}.
items.noLintian: lintian is not installed: its checks are left out.

send.descriptionPlaceholder: Package details, included changes or release notes...
send.emptyPackages: No .deb packages added. Drag files here or use the buttons above.
send.authRequiredDesc: You must configure a GitHub token with repository permissions before submitting proposals.
send.noTargetsDesc: To submit packages, you need to configure at least one destination repository.

proposals.acceptComment: Proposal accepted and added to the repository `{repo}`: the packages are signed and published.
proposals.rejectComment: Proposal rejected by the maintainer of the repository.
proposals.emptyText: When a team developer submits packages for this repository, they will appear here for review and approval.
proposals.acceptedNotice: Proposal #{number} accepted, signed, and published to main.
proposals.rejectExplanation: The Pull Request will be closed on GitHub. You can optionally specify a reason for the developer.
proposals.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Missing dependencies or failed verification...
proposals.acceptExplanation: {count} packages will be imported into {repo}, signed with GPG, and published to main.
proposals.cleanFirstHint: Useful when new builds do not replace the old ones by version: removes the packages of the pool before adding the new ones, so no obsolete leftovers stay.

accounts.noKeyringTitle: There is no keyring in this session
accounts.noKeyringDesc: Tokens are kept only in the keyring of the system. Install GNOME Keyring, KWallet or KeePassXC (with its Secret Service on), log in again and come back to add an account.
accounts.title: Accounts & Authentication
accounts.subtitle: Manage your GitHub account to submit packages and collaborate with the team.
accounts.disconnectConfirm: Are you sure you want to disconnect your GitHub account and delete the stored token?
accounts.tokenExplanation: To submit package proposals to remote repositories, you only need a GitHub Personal Access Token (classic) with the "repo" scope. You do not need local repositories or GPG keys.
accounts.step1: Sign in to GitHub and navigate to Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Tokens (classic).
accounts.step2: Generate a new token with the "repo" scope checked.
accounts.step3: Copy the token and paste it in the field below.
accounts.developerInfoTitle: Information for developers and package builders
accounts.developerInfoBody: You only need to configure your account here to submit compiled .deb packages to configured repositories from the Send tab.
accounts.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to remove this GitHub account?

targets.title: Publishing Destinations
targets.subtitle: Manage remote repositories where packages are published.
targets.emptyDesc: Add remote Git repositories to configure where the repository is published.
targets.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this destination?
